rundown: Wildcats beat Eagles 81-47 at Memorial Coliseum (KY) in Lexington, KY. Wildcats led 43-20 at the half and never looked back. The 1st quarter decided it: Wildcats won it 25-2. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 100%).
Leading the way — Eagles: Peyton Hill 16 pts; Anna Habra 3 ast, 8 reb. Wildcats: Clara Strack 29 pts, 18 reb; Maddyn Greenway 5 ast.
Where Wildcats won it: they shot 45% to 27%, shot 48% from three to 31% and won the boards 47-34.
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Wildcats closed as 47.5-point favorites and won but didn't cover (Eagles +47.5 cashed); the total closed at 140.5 and they combined for 128, under by 12.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 15, 11:58 AM ET. It had Eagles 0% and Wildcats 100%, projecting Eagles 51.1 – Wildcats 93.1 (144.2 total, Wildcats by 42).

Final: Eagles 47 – Wildcats 81. Right winner: it had Wildcats at 100%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Eagles came in with a 4% below average attack and a 4% leakier than average defense (0-3, 62 scored and 75.3 allowed a game over 3 games), worth about 159 and 160 games of evidence. Projected to score 51.1, they scored 47 (−4.1 points, 8% under); projected to allow 93.1, they allowed 81 (−12.1 points, 13% under).

Wildcats came in with a 20% above average attack and a 18% stingier than average defense (4-0, 88.8 scored and 44.5 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 180 and 178 games of evidence. Projected to score 93.1, they scored 81 (−12.1 points, 13% under); projected to allow 51.1, they allowed 47 (−4.1 points, 8% under).

The bigger miss was Wildcats' scoring (-12.1 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 128 against 144.2 projected (-16.2), about the 12th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14).

Margin: Wildcats by 34 against Wildcats by 42 projected, about the 27th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±13).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Market (Line movement signal): Wildcats ×1.02, Eagles ×1.00. It favored Wildcats, who did not beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:
UK -47.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 48% vs 50% fair (-1.7 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. EMU +47.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 52% vs 50% fair (+1.7 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close. OVER 140.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 51% vs 50% fair (+1.1 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. UNDER 140.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 49% vs 50% fair (-1.1 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body: The sharp side by the algo's read was Wildcats, who won and didn't cover.

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin.

The result was off its normal range without being an outlier, so the flags may have played a part.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.876 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -6.7 points. It counts toward NCAAW scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 537 graded NCAAW games the algo now scales scoring ×0.986 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: Eagles attack ×0.983, defense ×0.996 (3 games); Wildcats attack ×1.018, defense ×0.960 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
